newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola closes sharply higher to limit up.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola closes sharply higher to limit up.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed sharply higher to the $10.00 limit up on Friday supported by commercial buying sparked by soaring CBOT soybeans, floor sources said.
They noted volume was heavy with the buying absorbing fairly active hedging as the rise prompted a pick-up in producer sales. March canola closed $9.80 up at $412.00.

Flaxseed was also up sharply aided by spillover buying from other oilseed markets and talk of linseed oil sales to China. Details of any business were, however, scarce. March flaxseed finished up $8.00 at $362.00.

Western barley futures closed firmer but below the day's highs as late hedge selling trimmed gains. Dealers also said there was a lot of farmer selling interest around the $140.00 level, basis February futures.
February closed $1.30 higher at $137.00 after reaching a peak of $139.00.

Producer selling of feed wheat was also noted. March closed $2.20 higher at $176.00. Dealers noted that concern about tight stocks had prompted some commission houses to cover March shorts during the last few days.
March oats ended up $1.50 at $116.50 and May feed peas up $3.00 at $195.00.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
